cards.explanation: The answer is that a son's choices affect his parents. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (Proverbs 1:1), says a wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother. Either way, the son's choices land on the people who love him. Nobody's choices stay in their own little corner, friends.
The answer is righteousness, friends! The verse says it flat out: "…righteousness brings deliverance from death." Treasure gotten the wrong way profits nothing, but righteousness actually delivers.

The answer is False, friends. Solomon says, "The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but He denies the craving of the wicked." So the righteous are not left hungry, and the craving of the wicked is the thing He denies. Two sides of one line.

The answer is to work while the work is ready, friends. The son who gathers in summer is wise, and the son who sleeps during harvest is disgraceful. The harvest is ready now, so that's when the gathering gets done. A harvest doesn't wait around for anybody to wake up.

The answer is True, friends! "The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot." Both halves are about what's left behind: the memory and the name. One is remembered as a blessing, and the other rots. I'd want to be the first kind of memory in any kitchen.

The answer is False, friends. Solomon says, "…but he who perverts his ways will be found out." The one who bends his ways doesn't stay hidden. Meanwhile the one who walks in integrity walks securely, with nothing to dodge.

The word is covers, friends! "Hatred stirs up dissension, but love covers all transgressions." Hatred stirs the pot, and love goes the other way. Notice it says all transgressions, so love's covering is not small.

The answer is say, friends! The mouth and the lips keep showing up in these proverbs: the mouth of the wicked, foolish lips, the mouth of the righteous, the mouth of the fool. Mouths and lips are for speaking, so Solomon keeps his eye on what people say.

The answer is his fortified city, friends! Solomon says, "The wealth of the rich man is his fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor." A fortified city has walls, so wealth works like walls for the rich man. The proverb is honest about how poverty hits the poor, too.

The answer is where each one's earnings take them, friends. Solomon says the labor of the righteous leads to life, and the gain of the wicked brings punishment. He follows the labor of one and the gain of the other to where each ends up. Life on one side, punishment on the other.

The answer is False, friends. Solomon says, "Whoever heeds instruction is on the path to life, but he who ignores reproof goes astray." So the one who ignores reproof goes astray. Whoever heeds instruction is the one on the path to life.

The word is restrained, friends! Solomon says, "…he who restrains his lips is wise." When words are many, sin is unavoidable, so holding the lips back is the wise move. Sometimes the smartest thing in the room is a closed mouth.

The answer is that their words are worth a lot, friends! Choice silver is silver of high quality, so the tongue of the righteous is valuable. Solomon says, "The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the wicked has little worth." One side is worth a lot, and the other has little worth. Easy to see which one I'd want in my bakery.

The answer is judgment, friends. Solomon says, "The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of judgment." The righteous feed many with their lips, while fools die for lack of judgment. It's a hard line, but it's a clear one.

The answer is False, friends. Solomon says, "The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it." The blessing enriches, and the LORD adds no sorrow to it. So the idea that sorrow comes along with it doesn't match the verse.

The answer is that it will overtake him, friends. Solomon says, "What the wicked man dreads will overtake him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted." What he dreads catches up with him. On the other side, the righteous get what they desire.

The answer is False, friends. Solomon says, "When the whirlwind passes, the wicked are no more, but the righteous are secure forever." The whirlwind passes, the wicked are no more, and the righteous are still standing. Secure forever is a good place to be.

The answer is the slacker, friends! Solomon says, "Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the slacker to those who send him." Vinegar on your teeth, smoke in your eyes, that's what the slacker is to the ones who sent him. Ouch, what a picture.

The word is nothing, friends! Solomon says, "The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish." What the wicked are counting on perishes, so it comes to nothing. The righteous end up with joy.

The answer is destruction, friends. Solomon says, "The way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright, but destruction awaits those who do evil." The same way of the LORD that shelters the upright sits across from destruction. A refuge on one side, and on the other, something waiting.

The answer is True, friends. Solomon says, "The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut out." The mouth brings forth wisdom, and a perverse tongue is cut out. Words in these proverbs carry real consequences, and Solomon says it more than once in this chapter.
